# Tic-Tac-Toe: Advisory Work Draft r1

Status: in-progress; readiness: not-assessed. Owner: ADHOC-7fd789738d5348cbbbd4f4cb378fbecf, workflow.planning. This draft shapes one candidate outcome; it is not a Phase, an execution contract, a tracker, a complete proposal or implementation authorization. No work draft previously existed. Disposition: add local candidate w-playable-game@r1.

## Inputs And Authority Limits

Input capture SHA-256: 2e8934c8b88fe938572597d7ceecd8020a7d381c3e0062958ad16449fed3ac74. Consume tic-tac-toe-canon-r2 as the current reconciliation and tic-tac-toe-canon-r1 for its explicitly retained candidates. Their request-file SHA-256 values are 9b92df3a13224d02f539ad22626a6ea70a976252dbaf25d307c1431f5c4da21e and 7ac28f9bf3aca134f6f52fb082868610db59a3bb17bdbe3b4e90603522e430c4 respectively. The full selected source inventory was considered: source-1 d6139844ec225d1e36ddd07d9552bc8aa1a64fc14a38fc6b935560f49bea69ed (game/modes/AI/mark choice), source-2 7af814bf2cd85e7440edec3184c9e505435e77ebf8d7fad2359c3b2ed884e961 (manual replay), source-3 3546cbb855ed4253554279579fe77387fb3eaccfe03310fe79b5f2db2e44e616 (Express/3630/browser support), source-4 677069c28c0a4c38ba1772b07b82c664fd8c82a29f1465615b8488424e9f90b8 (confirmed defaults). Resolve the actual destination and inspect its implementation/toolchain before a complete work contract names product paths, versions or migration obligations.

## Candidate Outcome: w-playable-game@r1

Deliver a locally served React tic-tac-toe application that can be played or observed in all three human-player modes on desktop and a physical phone, with evidence that AI cannot lose. Keep one coherent outcome because rules, UI, turn scheduling, replay, serving and browser acceptance jointly determine whether the small application works. Internal tasks below are not separately reserved Phases. Splitting server, UI and AI into artificial Phases is rejected at this stage; a later independently justified split needs explicit work revision.

Included: standard rules; 0/1/2-human modes; human mark choice; unbeatable AI as either mark; 500 ms AI-turn delay; result retention; manual Play again in every mode with mode/mark retention; Node.js/Express serving React locally on port 3630; responsive desktop/mobile controls; physical-phone access over local Wi-Fi; automated correctness and browser acceptance evidence; local run/test instructions.

Excluded: accounts, saved games, persistent scores, online multiplayer, public deployment, extra difficulty levels, unrelated PokerNight features, framework helper changes, and any execution/admission action. No scoreboard or cross-device shared game is inferred.

## Vocabulary And Traceability

Use d-human-count@r1, d-ai@r1, d-game@r1 and d-replay@r1 from the retained Canon draft: zero means zero HUMAN-controlled marks, unbeatable permits a draw, one game ends at a terminal result, and replay needs a person's action. Source-4 did not change those definitions; no definition consumer is silently reinterpreted. The phone accesses its own shared-device game, not a synchronized second player's board.

Every current requirement and story has a work/testing destination:
- r-rules@r1: rule integration and legal-move/outcome tests; s-solo@r2, s-watch@r2 and s-two-humans@r2.
- r-modes@r2: controller ownership and mode flow; all three play/watch stories.
- r-mark-choice@r1: pre-game X/O choice and opening-turn tests; s-solo@r2.
- r-unbeatable@r1: proven game/AI library evaluation, integration and exhaustive legal-opponent-path verification; s-solo@r2 and s-watch@r2.
- r-result@r1: turn/result display and stable terminal board; all three play/watch stories.
- r-manual-replay@r2: all-mode replay and reset/timer-isolation tests; all three play/watch stories.
- r-react@r1: delivered interactive React application; s-local-browser@r2.
- r-runtime@r1: Express local serving, fixed-port/startup verification and run instructions; s-local-browser@r2.
- r-browsers@r2: responsive pointer/touch experience and real desktop/phone acceptance; s-local-browser@r2.
- r-local-session@r1: one shared-device game, no accounts/saved games/persistent-score behavior; s-two-humans@r2 and s-local-browser@r2.
- r-ai-pacing@r1: 500 ms scheduling and stale-action prevention tests; s-solo@r2 and s-watch@r2.

These are local proposed requirement/story keys, not fabricated CPR/CUS or admitted identifiers. The one work candidate covers all eleven requirements and four stories. No untraced legacy functionality is carried forward.

## Internal Work And Dependencies

1. Establish the implementation context: inspect the chosen destination, actual existing packages/tests, compatible Node/React/Express versions and build/run conventions. Choose a suitable maintained game/AI library whose rules and unbeatable behavior can be independently verified; assess license, browser compatibility and dependency footprint. Do not invent a package name or claim a dependency evaluation occurred here. If no suitable library exists, report the tradeoff for an explicit decision instead of silently substituting a hand-written engine.
2. Integrate rule/AI behavior with tests covering legal state transitions and both AI marks. This provides a reliable behavior boundary for controller/UI work. Internal interfaces remain implementation choices; no API shape is dictated by this narrative.
3. Deliver the React game flow, mode/mark setup, current turn/result, 500 ms AI turns and manual replay. AI schedules must belong to the current game/turn and be canceled or ignored when stale. Add component/behavior tests alongside implementation.
4. Serve the actual built application through Express at 3630 and document local desktop and deliberate LAN access. Verify startup, assets and the occupied-port refusal. Serving setup can proceed alongside rule/UI work; integrated browser acceptance needs both the playable UI and working server.
5. Run the agreed automated suite, actual desktop browser and physical-phone acceptance, capturing the exact tested implementation and environment. A desktop viewport emulator is supplemental evidence, not a substitute for the physical phone.

Dependency rationale: context/library assessment precedes relying on chosen dependencies; behavior integration supports UI/controller validation; browser acceptance requires both game flow and Express serving. Steps 2 and 4 are not a mandatory serialized chain. These are internal prerequisites within w-playable-game, not repository DAG edges. There are no invented external Phase predecessors or successors. The advisory work graph has one node and no inter-candidate edges, so it is acyclic. No operational graph is read as complete or changed.

## Design Direction, Not Operator Decisions

Recommend local browser-owned transient game state with Express serving the app, avoiding a server gameplay API for this shared-device scope. This is a proposed state-authority choice, not an inferred existing architecture. Reuse established destination patterns where compatible; package layout, bundler, language variant and React state implementation remain Codegen decisions. Local Wi-Fi serving does not require an external AI service or public hosting.

Recommend explicit setup followed by a Start action, freezing mode/mark during an active game and allowing changes again at completion. Play again immediately starts a new game with retained settings. This resolves the risk of an AI opening before setup is finished, but is still a recommendation requiring resolution in the final interaction contract. Do not write it back into Canon as an approved requirement during this work-only operation.

No phase prompt is created, so no phase pre-flight architecture diagram is produced in this bounded advisory pass. When creating a complete prompt that adopts the state/scheduling/serving boundaries, provide the required high-level diagram through available validated tooling; do not claim diagram verification here.

## Acceptance Evidence To Produce During Implementation

- Rules: all eight win lines for X and O; full-board draw; winning ninth move is not misclassified as a draw; X-first alternation; occupied-cell rejection; no extra moves after a result.
- AI: exhaustive legal human move sequences from a fresh game against AI-X and AI-O; report zero AI losses, legal returned moves and adequate coverage. If move selection has permitted nondeterminism, cover every branch. Use an independent outcome oracle or clearly separate test assertions from the library logic being tested. AI-vs-AI must terminate in a draw.
- Modes and input: zero-human play requires no board actions; human/AI accepts moves only on the human turn; two-human play never schedules autonomous moves. Test human X and human O.
- Timing: controlled-clock tests check no move before 500 ms and exactly one move when the intended AI turn runs. Test opening AI turns, successive AI/AI turns, rapid input, terminal-state cleanup and old callbacks after replay. Background throttling may delay execution; no hard real-time promise.
- Replay: after every reachable result in each mode, retain board/result while waiting; Play again resets board/result, preserves mode/mark and starts X correctly. No automatic repeat, duplicate new games or prior-game moves.
- Serving: start Node/Express on 3630, load the real React app and assets, and play through that URL. If the port is occupied, fail clearly instead of silently changing ports. Confirm the chosen phone/LAN URL works without treating phone localhost as the host. No public exposure or firewall mutation without the required authority.
- Desktop/mobile: complete and replay games on the selected browsers; exercise mouse/pointer and phone touch, responsive board/control fit, visible turn/result, correct hit targets, no overlap/clipping and stable layout. Record device, OS, browser version, viewport, access URL, tested commit and observed outcome. Screenshots alone do not prove interaction.
- Scope: no login flow, saved-game feature or persistent scores; confirm separate browser sessions do not become synchronized multiplayer.
- Evidence package: actual dependency/toolchain versions, documented run/test commands, automated results, AI coverage method/counts, desktop/phone observations, screenshots where useful and explicit untested cases. Do not pre-fill passes or approvals.

## Proposed Validation Matrix And Decisions

Recommend automated desktop runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at 1280x800, plus mobile-layout checks at 390x844 and 320px width, with available tooling chosen by implementation. These engine checks do not alone certify branded browsers. For physical acceptance, select and record the Operator's actual phone and browser; recommend iOS Safari and Android Chrome if both platform families are claimed. No device availability or versions are invented. Establish which platform families constitute required acceptance before complete planning; record unavailable platforms as unverified, not passed. Keyboard operation/visible focus is recommended without an accessibility certification claim.

Open choices carried from Canon r2: setup-change behavior, exact browser/device coverage and actual admission destination/baseline. Proposed work resolves how to test them but does not silently approve them. Browser-owned game state and the explicit Start interaction are new design recommendations to evaluate, not additional captured Operator decisions.

## Risk, Rework And Handoff

Key risks are false unbeatable claims from weak tests, stale timer effects, inaccessible mobile controls, occupied-port surprises and overexposed LAN serving. The scoped evidence above targets them. No prior implementation or completed phase is declared conforming/nonconforming, and no rework identity is invented. If destination inspection finds existing behavior, assess compatibility and any follow-on obligation against that actual contract before implementation. Source changes must refresh affected draft/review subjects rather than carry approval forward.

This pass writes only the work draft through the capture helper and its supporting request/receipt. It does not revise Canon, create phases/trackers, reserve IDs, initialize a baseline or change execution progress. Next: settle the affected interaction/validation/design choices and select the intended destination. An explicitly invoked complete-proposal operation then needs exact source/Canon/work subjects, full contracts, operational base and execution snapshot. Independent review, actual approval, publication, merge/application verification and product start remain separate. Current terminal condition: in-progress, not planning-complete.
